comment: Real repositories, pinned by commit. Chosen for variety of shape rather
than fame: ecosystem, age, activity, and how badly they break an
assumption. Add entries freely; each one costs about a second.
Run `python3 -m tests.corpus --sync` to populate the cache.

repositories.note: C, two files, twenty commits, dormant since 2016. The smallest real thing.
No program at all. Thousands of commits over a tree of templates.
Go, multi module, deliberately tidy. The well-behaved case.
JavaScript from 2009. Long history, many authors, committed build output.
Go, single purpose, quiet for years. Tests the dormancy bands.
Python, mature, maintained. Modern packaging metadata.
Python, six thousand commits, hundreds of authors. Bus factor and fix ratio.
Ruby and shell mixed, long lived. Language attribution across two families.
Rust, active, lockfile committed. The healthy modern case.
JavaScript, four files. Small enough to reason about by hand.
